newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's 1230 GMT release of the U.S. July international trade report, dealers said on Wednesday.
The international trade figures for July is forecast to show a gap of US$8.8 billion compared with a US$8.1 billion shortfall reported in June.
"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's international trade numbers for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday and Thursday/Friday eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.
But three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, six-months went up 1/16 point to 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months increased 1/16 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
"But market focus is still on the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on September 24," he said.

There's some uncertainty in the market following reports that an unnamed senior U.S. Fed official told Reuters on Tuesday that eight of the Federal Reserve's 12 district banks have requested a hike in the discount rate and the fed fund rate.

"There's some speculation in the market that the Fed might raise its rates by about 25 basis points following comments this morning by Fed officials that the Fed might raise its rates by around 25 basis point at next week's (FOMC) meeting," another dealer said.
